description: Agent Waste and Recycling Records: submit a waste manifest record with the hauler permit, facility, receiving and disposal records it answers to: the manifest record with its reference, the waste generator and the period; each hauler the permit record lists with its id, permit reference and name; each facility the facility record lists with its id, reference and name; each facility receiving record with its id, reference, the manifest it receives, the facility, the quantity received and the moment received; each disposal record entry with its id, reference, the manifest it disposes of, the quantity disposed and the moment disposed; each manifest entry with its id, manifest number, hauler, generator, waste type, quantity shipped, receiving facility and the moment shipped. The signed report gives the manifests and the records behind them, each manifest’s hauler against the permit record, each manifest’s quantity against the totals the disposal record holds for it, each shipment against a receiving facility record naming it, and each entry against the fields the record format requires, and counts them, and names divergent manifest records: a manifest naming a hauler the permit record does not list, a manifest quantity the disposal record’s totals do not reflect, a shipment with no receiving facility record behind it, and a manifest entry missing the fields the record format requires; then a manifest naming a receiving facility the facility record does not list and a receiving record naming a manifest the manifest record does not hold, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No manifest entries, no permit record beside manifests that name a hauler, no disposal record beside manifest quantities, or no receiving records beside shipments leaves those points unverified. Manifests, permits and facilities match by letters and digits, so WM-0412 and WM 0412 are one manifest, haulers match by permit reference or name, and quantities read to the hundredth in the unit the records use. This reads the waste manifest record as a whole: review_mcp_manifest reads an MCP server’s tool declarations, while the manifest check reads whether every waste shipment moved under a permitted hauler, reached a receiving facility and was disposed of in the quantity shipped. Verdict waste_manifest_divergent, waste_manifest_partial, waste_manifest_unverified or waste_manifest_consistent. POST /api/waste-manifest-check. Reads the waste and recycling records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the records as supplied only: it hauls no waste, operates no facility, contacts no regulator, hauler or disposal site and issues no permit or certification, which stay with the waste operation, its haulers, its facilities and its regulators, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Waste and Recycling Records reads a waste operation’s own records: waste manifest records, hauler permit records, disposal and landfill records, recycling processing records, diversion and recovery records, pickup and collection log records, facility and scale records and contamination report records, each against the hauler permit, facility, receiving and disposal records, the waste types, areas and dates in the pickup log, the manifests and the dates the record states, the inbound, outbound and residue records, the processing, reuse, disposal and pickup totals, the service record, the scale tickets and dispositions, or the follow-up entries and the inspected load counts on record. The family’s ground is the paper trail behind the waste stream: what the manifest shows, what the disposal record supports, what the permits cover, and whether the diversion claims and pickup logs hold up; it reads records about waste streams and the people who move them, not live environmental monitoring and not cleanup services: the Agent Energy family reads utility and generation records, the Agent Agriculture Records family reads a farm’s production records, the Agent Food Safety Records family reads a food business’s safety file and the Agent Aviation Records family reads an air operator’s flight and maintenance paper trail, while this family reads a waste operation’s own records and reads none of those. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-waste-recycling-records-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-waste-recycling-records/.
